items.elements: One longer, slightly falling opening note around 3-4 kHz (0.27-0.5 s). Then five short, evenly spaced, sharp hooked chips at about 3.7 kHz (0.62-1.15 s). Then a steep down-slur from about 8 to 5 kHz that runs straight into a long, flat, buzzy trill at about 4.7 kHz with roughly 11 pulses (1.3-1.78 s).
items.phrase: Oh, pick pick pick pick pick, see-shiverrrr
items.grounds: The long opening note became a drawn-out 'Oh', the five identical short chips became five 'pick's, and the falling slur into a flat pulsing trill became 'see' falling into a rolled 'shiver'. None of the words came from the familiar 'drink-your-tea' mnemonic, though I know it, and this cut does not match it well because it has five chips instead of one or two.

items.elements: Nine repeated two-part units, about 0.3 s apart, that grow louder through the song. Each unit is a thin high stroke at about 4.6-6 kHz followed by a hooked down-sweep to about 3 kHz. A faint lower falling note ends the song at about 2.9 s.
items.phrase: Peter Peter Peter Peter Peter Peter Peter Peter Peter
items.grounds: Each unit is two strokes, a high, light first one and a lower, heavier falling second one, so I used a two-syllable word stressed on the first syllable, nine times, getting louder. The word choice and the stress pattern were influenced by the 'teacher, teacher' mnemonic I already knew for this species.

items.elements: Five short notes in a row, each rising sharply to about 6.5 kHz and then dropping to about 5 kHz (0.22-0.98 s). Then one higher note falling from about 9 to 6 kHz (1.07 s). Then two notes sweeping up from about 3 to 6.5 kHz (1.15-1.55 s), and a final loud, long down-slur from about 9 to 3 kHz (1.6-1.75 s).
items.phrase: tip tip tip tip tip, TIP, why? why? DOWN
items.grounds: The five matching short notes became 'tip' repeated, the single higher note became a stressed 'TIP', the two upward sweeps became the question 'why?' twice, and the big final fall became an emphatic 'DOWN'. I deliberately avoided the 'pleased to meet you' mnemonic I know, but knowing it probably made me notice the strong accented ending.

items.elements: The main singer starts at about 1.3 s with a flat, rough, buzzy note at about 3.5 kHz. Next comes a sharp upward sweep that reaches 5-10 kHz (1.62-1.75 s), then a short falling note to end (1.78-1.83 s). Two fainter phrases, each a rise then a fall, come before it (0-1.05 s) and look like a different or more distant bird.
items.grounds: The buzzy flat note became 'fizz', the loud high upsweep became the stressed 'BEER', and the short drop became 'oh'. 'BEER' came from the 'free beer' mnemonic I already knew, not only from the picture.

items.elements: Two long, slow upward slurs from about 1.8 to 3.2 kHz (0.2-0.6 s and 0.95-1.45 s). Then five short, evenly spaced down-slurs from about 3.5 to 1.8 kHz (1.55-3.0 s), each with a clear harmonic above it.
items.phrase: Whyyy? Whyyy? here, here, here, here, here
items.grounds: The two long rising sounds read as drawn-out questions, 'Whyyy?', and the five quick falling notes became five clipped, downward 'here's. I avoided the 'birdie birdie' and 'cheer cheer' mnemonics I know, though 'here' sounds close to 'cheer'.
